questions.question: If a scientist tests a substance using chromatography and it only produces a single spot on the chromatogram, what does this indicate about the substance?
options: It is a mixture of several different dyes.
It is a pure substance.
It is highly insoluble in the mobile phase.
It has reacted with the pencil line.

questions.question: Why is a pencil used to draw the starting line on a chromatogram instead of a pen?
options: Pencil lead is insoluble in water and will not run with the solvent.
Pencil lead reacts with the chromatography paper to stay in place.
Ink from a pen is too heavy to travel up the paper.
Pencil lines can easily be erased if an error is made.

questions.question: Under what circumstances would you choose fractional distillation over simple distillation?
options: When separating an insoluble solid from a highly viscous liquid.
When separating immiscible liquids that naturally form distinct layers.
When separating mixtures with three or more substances, or substances with similar boiling points.
When you want to extract a soluble solid from its solvent completely.

questions.question: What is the primary consequence if the condenser in a distillation apparatus is allowed to warm up?
options: The rate of vaporization inside the flask will decrease rapidly.
The condenser becomes less effective, allowing more gas to escape.
The distillate will instantly freeze inside the delivery tube.
The boiling point of the remaining mixture will significantly increase.

questions.question: How does the rate of solvent evaporation affect the size of crystals formed during crystallisation?
options: Faster evaporation leads to much larger, more defined crystals.
Slower evaporation allows larger crystals to form.
The rate of evaporation has no effect on final crystal size.
Evaporation must be stopped completely for any crystals to grow.

questions.question: Which of the following mixtures could be separated by using a magnet?
options: A mixture of copper filings and aluminum powder.
A mixture of sand and salt crystals.
A mixture of iron filings and sulfur powder.
A mixture of zinc pieces and plastic beads.

questions.question: What is the purpose of adding a drop of water to the filter paper inside a filter funnel before filtering?
options: It helps keep the filter paper cone open and stuck to the funnel for easy filtering.
It chemically reacts with the paper to make it completely waterproof.
It dissolves any fine particles on the paper to prevent clogging.
It speeds up the chemical reaction between the solute and the solvent.

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of immiscible liquids when they are mixed together and allowed to settle?
options: They chemically combine to form a brand new single liquid substance.
They do not mix, and the less dense liquid will float above the other.
They completely dissolve in each other to form a clear, uniform solution.
They instantly react and produce a solid precipitate at the bottom.

questions.question: Which statement is true about miscible liquids when they are left undisturbed?
options: They will slowly separate into distinct layers based on density.
They do not separate into layers over time.
The lighter liquid will eventually evaporate completely, leaving the heavier one.
They will react to form an insoluble solid that sinks to the bottom.

questions.question: Which sequence of processes is correct for separating pure salt from a sample of rock salt?
options: Simple distillation, fractional distillation, followed by decanting.
Making a solution, filtration, and then crystallisation.
Magnetism, chromatography, followed by evaporation to dryness.
Centrifuging, decanting, and then simple distillation.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep a condenser cold during the distillation process?
options: To prevent the glass from cracking due to high pressure.
To speed up the condensation of the vapor back into a liquid.
To ensure the distillate does not catch fire on contact with air.
To lower the boiling point of the mixture in the round-bottom flask.

questions.question: If an unknown liquid is analyzed using paper chromatography and produces three distinct spots, what does this tell you?
options: The liquid is a pure compound.
The liquid is a mixture of different substances.
The solvent was contaminated with insoluble impurities.
The paper was folded incorrectly during the experiment.

questions.question: During the process of crystallisation, where does the solvent go as the solute begins to reform?
options: It is absorbed into the solid crystals being formed.
It evaporates into the air around you.
It chemically decomposes into oxygen and hydrogen gases.
It drains through the bottom of the evaporating basin.

questions.question: What is the purity status of the liquid collected as distillate at the end of a successful simple distillation?
options: It is a concentrated mixture of all volatile components.
It remains a solution containing a small amount of solid solute.
It is a pure liquid.
It is an unstable emulsion of different liquids.

questions.question: When would simple distillation be the most appropriate separation method to use?
options: When separating a mixture that contains only two substances with significantly different boiling points.
When separating a mixture of five different gases with similar boiling points.
When separating insoluble sand from a mixture of salt and water.
When separating immiscible liquids like oil and water.
